- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–15% if recent sentiment is negative.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2 days above true peak, then allow gradual decline.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags in adjusting downward; apply downward bias starting 3–5 days after sentiment shift.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day windows; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 2–5% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment is positive but price is falling, model often overestimates recovery; reduce forecast by 3–8% if sentiment positive but price trend is downward.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate volatility in early days; apply smoothing filter to first 7 days of forecast if sentiment is volatile.
